# JPEG metadata segment fixtures

Generated by `python3 scripts/make-jpeg-segment-fixtures.py` using the Python
standard library. Tiny 3×2 JPEGs use the project's synthetic pixel/EXIF inputs.
The grayscale base is a recorded `cjpeg -quality 90 -optimize` encoding of
invented PGM samples; no external tool is required to regenerate these files.
ICC matrix/TRC data and XMP strings are invented for transport tests, not
calibrated camera profiles or real photographs. No third-party profiles are
imported.

| Fixture | Metadata |
| --- | --- |
| `exif_only.jpg` | EXIF with Orientation 6, synthetic camera/exposure/GPS values and opaque MakerNotes |
| `icc_only.jpg` | One ICC chunk |
| `xmp_only.jpg` | Standard Adobe XMP |
| `all_metadata.jpg` | EXIF + ICC + standard XMP |
| `icc_multi.jpg` | Three ICC chunks in physical order 3, 1, 2, interleaved with EXIF/XMP |
| `icc_bad_sequence.jpg` | Chunk 1 declares a two-chunk profile, but chunk 2 is absent |
| `no_metadata.jpg` | RGB baseline without preserved metadata |
| `gray_no_metadata.jpg` | Grayscale baseline without preserved metadata |
| `gray_icc.jpg` | One-component grayscale JPEG with an invented gray ICC profile |
| `xmp_extended.jpg` | Standard XMP referencing two Extended XMP chunks in reverse offset order, plus EXIF/ICC |

Additional malformed, maximum-length, post-scan, and memory-limit cases are
generated in disposable test directories. These fixtures live separately from
`../jpeg/` to preserve the existing collection-statistics snapshots.
